_readme: THE ROUTING VOCABULARY (DRE-2724). One file, read by everything.
A verdict is a ROUTING DECISION, not a quality score. It answers *who
builds this, and how* — and every answer sends the card somewhere
different. Framed as a score a critic drifts toward marking things good so
it looks useful; framed as routing there is no good or bad, only a wrong
destination, which shows up immediately.
Per verdict: what it means, the LANE it sends the card to, the ACTOR
accountable for it there, whether the sweep may promote it, and the labels
the stamp applies. Destination and actor are both drawn from
config/lane-contract.json — a destination that is not a lane, or an actor
that is not a permitted writer OF THAT LANE, is a dead end, and the
amendment to this card was written because OPERATOR and WORKBENCH had
exactly that: 'enters Backlog and goes to the queue when its turn comes',
with no turn ever coming (DRE-2735 — the promoter skips a parentless card,
and it skips a non-FLEET verdict too).
ACTOR is per-lane, not global (DRE-2824). PARKED named `operator` on
`Backlog`, a lane whose permitted writers are all process — so a PARKED
card was sent to a lane the actor named to handle it may not write. Backlog
is process-controlled now: every card enters through Intake, and `operator`
is deliberately NOT added back to Backlog's writers. `operator` was in the
field to carry 'only a human revives it'; that is a separate, later human
act, and it now has its own `revival` field. The actor is who handles the
card at the destination — or, where the point of the verdict is that nobody
does, the writer that performs the move. All five were re-checked against
the lane contract when this changed; only PARKED was wrong.
JSON, not YAML: scripts/reconcile.py imports the reader on every product
repo's sweep, where there is no pip install and PyYAML is not guaranteed.
Regenerate the document after any edit:
python3 scripts/routing_verdict.py render
Check this file against the lane contract and its own fixtures:
python3 scripts/routing_verdict.py check

verdicts.name: FLEET
verdicts.means: Buildable unattended in one pull request.
verdicts.why: The sweep promotes it out of Backlog and the relay dispatches a build run. This is the only verdict that may be dispatched.

verdicts.name: WORKBENCH
verdicts.means: Needs an interactive flow or live system state — driving an auth flow, forcing a token past expiry, confirming something in production.
verdicts.why: It is real work and it goes on the board where work goes — but a person does it at an interactive session, so it carries `hand-built`, which is already the signal that stops the sweep dispatching a competing run or reporting the card as stranded (DRE-2524). Backlog was the old answer and Backlog is a dead end: nothing there ever moves a non-FLEET card on.

verdicts.name: OPERATOR
verdicts.means: Not code — a deploy, a migration run, a secret.
verdicts.why: Same destination as WORKBENCH and the same actor, because the same person does it; the difference is that no code is produced. `no-code` is the existing marker for that, and it already stops a merged runbook auto-closing the card (linear_ops.auto_done_skip_reason — six false portico closes).

verdicts.name: PARKED
verdicts.means: Well-formed and deliberately not to be built.
verdicts.why: Backlog IS the right lane for a card that is deliberately inert — the dead end is the point. It is never promoted and never reported as stalled by any sweep. The actor is the planning-exit writer that stamps this verdict and lands the card there, because Backlog is a lane only the process writes; it is not somebody waiting to pick the card up, because for PARKED nobody is.
verdicts.revival: Only a human revives a PARKED card. Nothing in the pipeline takes it back out of Backlog — no sweep, no run, no label — so a person deciding the card is worth building again is a separate, later act, and never the actor of this routing decision.

verdicts.name: NEEDS WORK
verdicts.why: It returns to Planning with the specific missing thing named — the verdict comment carries it, so the planner is told what to add rather than asked to guess.

precedence: An explicit role label — read first, no judgement.
The title convention — anchored at the start of the title, never a substring search.
The acceptance-criteria rule: can an unattended agent SATISFY the stated exit condition?
Only what survives all three reaches a judgement call, and only then is a model asked.

_readme: Precedence 1. An exact label match, lower-cased — never a prefix: `no-codegen`
is not `no-code`, and reading it as one is the same mistake class as a
substring blocker match, one field over.

title_conventions.means: The card's deliverable is a human's sign-off on live work.
title_conventions.example: SIGN-OFF (OPERATOR): rotate the CloudFront key group
adversarial: Add a SIGN-OFF (OPERATOR) section to the runbook template
Runbook: the SIGN-OFF (OPERATOR) checklist is out of date

title_conventions.means: The card closes only when every end-state claim in its demo report is a PASS — somebody drives the live system and records what it did. That is an interactive flow over live state, which is WORKBENCH; it is not a deploy, so it is not OPERATOR.
title_conventions.example: DEMO: Phase 3 — folder access end to end

_readme: Precedence 3, and the whole mechanical rule: route on whether an
unattended agent can SATISFY the acceptance criteria, not on whether it
could write the code. That reads the card's own stated exit condition
instead of guessing from the title.
Scoped to checkbox criteria ONLY, never free prose, and matched on whole
words. A bare substring match over prose is how epic DRE-2492 was jammed
by its own sentence 'neither depends on the other' for five days.
Order is load-bearing: interactive wins over visual. Screenshotting a
screen is not driving a flow, but driving a flow that ends at a screen is
still driving a flow.
EVERY PHRASE NAMES A REAL CARD THAT WRITES IT (DRE-2831). The first
version of this block was written from phrases a card author imagined,
and six of the nine static_visual phrases appear in ZERO of the 1,561
carded issues in this workspace — so the FLEET half almost never fired,
and real UI cards were routed by a model, at cost, on the exact case the
rule was supposed to decide for free. The remedy is not a longer guessed
list, which is the same defect made longer: it is the 'evidence' block on
each signal, which config_problems() refuses to let a phrase into the
vocabulary without. The verbatim criteria behind every phrase, the real
card bodies they were read from, and the measured before/after are in
tests/fixtures/routing-criteria-corpus-2026-08-31.json.

interactive.why: The criterion names an interactive flow or live system state. An unattended agent has no browser session, no live console and no clock it can move.

evidence.corpus: every issue in the Linear DRE workspace — 2,773 cards, 1,561 of them carrying `- [ ]` acceptance criteria
evidence.note: Attested the same way as the visual half, and seven phrases went the same way as its guesses: 'log out', 'force the token', 'past expiry', 'walk through', 'step through', 'in the browser' and 'interactively' matched no card at all and were dropped, and two more — 'past `exp`' and 'confirm the session' — matched only cards 'sign in' already catches, or a pytest session ('confirm the session fails with the expected error') — this workspace writes 'by hand' (24 cards) and 'manually' (10). 'in the live product' and 'verified live' were ADDED, and only because the visual half was widened: a criterion that states a rendered outcome and then says it is verified in the running product must reach a person, and interactive is read first.

static_visual.why: The criterion states a RENDERED OUTCOME, and static visual fidelity is FLEET-checkable: the agent's own suite asserts the render, and where the surface is a screen, qa-review.yml runs a visual-QA stage (DRE-1481) that installs chromium via Playwright, screenshots the changed screens, and hands the critic both the design PNG and the render, with the instruction to read both images and compare.

evidence.corpus: every issue in the Linear DRE workspace — 2,773 cards, 1,561 of them carrying `- [ ]` acceptance criteria
evidence.note: How this workspace really writes a visual criterion: 'Overview body renders Description, Equipment card, Evidence thumbnails' (DRE-1829), 'No hardcoded hex — all colors via design tokens' (DRE-1289). Two frequent candidates were tested and REJECTED rather than added: 'shows' (189 cards) reads the same on 'synth shows' and 'the log shows', so it cannot tell a screen from a CLI; the bare 'render' (95 cards) names an action or an endpoint — 'GET /d/{docId}/render' — rather than an outcome. Frequency alone is not evidence.

_readme: 'Could an agent build this unattended' is meaningless for a card the
planner owns. An epic gets a PLAN test — never a buildability test, and
never one of the five routes.
plan_test: it states an acceptance criterion for the set
